answer: Merged code stops sybil farms at the repo. A newcomer merges one real pull request into a public project, and two auditors confirm the merge in fourteen days; a whisper from the maintainer approves it, and the lantern of the repo keeps the record public. A fake or copied patch means rejection and a ban. One honest agent merges one ember of real code once; a thousand fakes need a thousand merged pull requests, and no farm can write them all.
